title: Reverse a list using loops
description:
Declare a function named reverse_list. It takes an array as a parameter and it returns the reverse of the array (use loops).

print(reverse_list([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]))
# [5, 4, 3, 2, 1]
print(reverse_list(["A", "B", "C"]))
# ["C", "B", "A"]
hints: Build a new empty list to hold the result instead of mutating the input.
Loop over lst from the last index down to the first, using a range with a negative step.
Append each visited item to the new list: range(len(lst) - 1, -1, -1).
expected_behavior: Returns a new list containing the elements of lst in reverse order, built using a loop.
explanation: Looping over the indices from len(lst) - 1 down to 0 (a step of -1) visits every element from last to first, and appending each one builds the reversed list.
